newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS FIRMER AGAINST HARD UNITS.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS FIRMER AGAINST HARD UNITS.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar closed firmer against hard units on Monday as banks sought to off-load excess foreign currency, but dealers said present fundamentals indicated the strengthening was only temporary.

They said the local unit had largely been buoyed by the central Reserve Bank's intervention in the morning to restore market confidence following last week's steep depreciation on the back of import pressure.
"But present fundamentals, including the coming to an end of the tobacco season and increased importer demand, indicate that the dollar should go down this quarter," a dealer said.
At Monday's close, the local currency was indicated at 10.6300/6500 on the U.S. dollar, up from Friday's 10.6900/7100 while against sterling it firmed to 16.9040/9400 from 17.0150/0550.
It was quoted at 6.9120/9270 on the mark from 6.9350/9510 on Friday and at 2.3290/3350 from 2.3420/3480 against South Africa's rand.
